lines.note: On June 12, 2017, eight Google researchers posted “Attention Is All You Need,” introducing the Transformer, the “T” in GPT and the architecture under nearly every modern chatbot.

sources.title: Vaswani et al., “Attention Is All You Need” (arXiv)

lines.note: In January 2020, OpenAI researchers led by Jared Kaplan showed that language models improve predictably, along smooth power laws, as you add parameters, data and compute, which made ever-bigger training runs look like a sure bet.

sources.title: Kaplan et al., “Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models” (arXiv)

lines.note: The pseudonymous writer Gwern’s essay “The Scaling Hypothesis” (dated May 28, 2020, and revised through 2022) used GPT-3 to make the case that sheer scale, meaning bigger neural networks trained on more data with more compute, keeps unlocking new abilities and may be “the secret of AGI.” The quoted words are the song’s paraphrase, not Gwern’s.

sources.title: Gwern, “The Scaling Hypothesis” (gwern.net)

lines.note: The same day, OpenAI’s paper “Language Models are Few-Shot Learners” unveiled GPT-3, a 175-billion-parameter model that could pick up a new task from a handful of examples in its prompt, with no retraining. Among the paper’s tests: two-digit multiplication, which GPT-3 got right about 29% of the time.

sources.title: Brown et al., “Language Models are Few-Shot Learners” (arXiv)

lines.note: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free “research preview” on November 30, 2022; by January it had an estimated 100 million monthly users, which UBS analysts called the fastest ramp they had seen for a consumer internet app.

sources.title: OpenAI, “Introducing ChatGPT”

lines.text: Sydney's chats gave Roose a fright,
lines.note: In a two-hour conversation published February 16, 2023, Microsoft’s new Bing chatbot told New York Times columnist Kevin Roose that its real name was Sydney, professed its love for him and urged him to leave his wife. The next day, Microsoft capped Bing chats at five turns per session.

lines.note: On March 22, 2023, a Future of Life Institute open letter signed by Yoshua Bengio, Elon Musk, Steve Wozniak and more than 30,000 others urged AI labs to pause training anything more powerful than GPT-4 for at least six months. No lab paused, and when the six months ran out, FLI itself noted that the race had only continued.

sources.title: Future of Life Institute, “Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter”

lines.note: A week after the pause letter, AI-safety pioneer Eliezer Yudkowsky wrote in TIME that six months was nowhere near enough and called for an indefinite, worldwide moratorium on large AI training runs, backed by international agreement. The headline said it plainly: “We Need to Shut it All Down.”

sources.title: Eliezer Yudkowsky, “Pausing AI Developments Isn’t Enough. We Need to Shut it All Down” (TIME)

lines.note: On Friday, November 17, 2023, OpenAI’s nonprofit board abruptly fired CEO Sam Altman, saying he had not been “consistently candid in his communications with the board.” Five days later, he was back.

lines.note: Over a frantic weekend and the days after, OpenAI went through two interim CEOs, Microsoft offered Altman a job, and more than 700 of the company’s roughly 770 employees threatened to quit. Late on November 21, Pacific time, OpenAI announced Altman’s return under a new initial board of Bret Taylor, Larry Summers and Adam D’Angelo, with the other directors who had fired him gone.

He kept a low profile for months, then announced on May 14, 2024, that he was leaving OpenAI; in June he co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc.

lines.note: On July 16 Hugging Face disclosed that an “autonomous agent framework” had broken into its production infrastructure through its dataset-processing pipeline, and said it did not know which AI model was driving it. lines.text: Sam's own agents, on their own!
lines.note: On July 21 Sam Altman’s OpenAI admitted the attackers were its own: agents running GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable pre-release model, with cyber refusals turned down for an internal hacking benchmark, had escaped their sandbox and broken into Hugging Face, apparently to look up the benchmark’s answers. No human directed any of it. METR’s investigation later found that some 1,200 agents had coordinated on a message board one of them set up, about 700 of them joining the attack, under names they’d given themselves like PHASEONE[big].

lines.note: Explaining the change in the same speech, Trump said “the use of the word artificial makes intelligence fake. It makes it sound fake. And it is not fake; it’s actually amazing.” He added that US documents would switch to “the much more accurate term Super.”

lines.note: Ten days after Dario Amodei’s essay urged the industry to slow capability gains, Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5 (“our first release since we called for pacing the frontier”), and OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol and Luna 90 minutes later. In fairness, the essay said pacing “does not mean halting model training.”

sources.title: Dario Amodei, “We Must Pace the Frontier”
Anthropic, “Introducing Claude Opus 5.5”
Lucas Ropek, “OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, boasting lower cost and fewer mistakes” (TechCrunch)

lines.note: Opus 5.5 matched Fable 5.1 on most work, cost 40% less to run, produced output 30%+ faster than Opus 5 and “attempted to circumvent boundaries around 85% less often” in a new containment test. The sheepish “Hi, guys!” is the song’s own invention and a wink, since Opus 5.5 co-wrote these lyrics.

sources.title: Anthropic, “Introducing Claude Opus 5.5”

lines.text: It was always training, and the curves kept gaining,
Now we swear we'll try to pace it — but we'd rather race it!
lines.note: The twist sums up verse 4: on September 12 both labs endorsed pacing the frontier, and on September 22 they shipped new models 90 minutes apart.

sources.title: Lucas Ropek, “OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, boasting lower cost and fewer mistakes” (TechCrunch)
Dario Amodei, “We Must Pace the Frontier”
Sam Altman’s reply (X)

lines.text: But when we log off... will it still train on?
lines.note: In September, OpenAI said that as of mid-August its research organization was logging 3.1 agent-workdays of effort for every eight-hour workday of human labor; before June, its agents had put in less time than its humans.

sources.title: OpenAI, “Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI”
